maml:description.maml:para: Returns reference data describing the identifiers expected for each discovered account Type/SubType.

Returns the CyberArk discovered account Type/SubType to identifiers mapping table, sourced from Types of accounts that can be sent via API (https://docs.cyberark.com/manage/latest/en/content/discovery/discovery-apis/discovery-api-types.htm).
For each Type/SubType combination, the returned object describes the mandatory Identifiers, any OptionalIdentifiers, and Notes explaining any known limitation.

A small number of rows in the source documentation describe an identifier only in prose (e.g. AWS's "AWS Account ID"), rather than giving the literal field name expected by the API. Those identifiers are intentionally omitted from Identifiers/OptionalIdentifiers rather than guessed at - Notes explains which identifier is affected on those rows. This does not stop you from including such an identifier yourself, if you separately know the correct field name to use - the -identifiers parameter of New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject, Test-DMDiscoveredLocalAccount & Add-DMDiscoveredLocalAccount always accepts any keys you provide; this command only describes what is confidently known, and drives their -type/-subType tab-completion and shape-mismatch warnings.

maml:description.maml:para: Updates an existing discovery scan definition.
Updates an existing scan definition used to discover accounts in target machines.
Any property not passed as a parameter is left unchanged, retaining its current value from the existing scan definition, so the update does not clear properties which are not being modified.
The scan type (-type) and location type (-locationType) of an existing scan definition cannot actually be changed by the API once set, even if different values are supplied here.

The required/valid keys of the `-properties` hashtable (and, for some scan types, whether `-networkId` is required) depend on the value of `-type`. Similarly, the required keys of `-recurrenceData` depend on the value of `-recurrenceType`. See the linked CyberArk API documentation for the full set of supported scan types and their properties/credentials/ recurrenceData shapes. Passing `-properties`/`-recurrenceData`/`-credentials` replaces the existing value entirely, rather than merging into it.
The id of the scan definition to update.
The name of the scan definition.
If not specified, the existing name of the scan definition is left unchanged.
Whether the scan is in an active or inactive state. If a scan is inactive, no scan instances can run from it.
If not specified, the existing state of the scan definition is left unchanged.
The scan type of this scan definition.
This value cannot actually be changed once a scan definition is created; if not specified, the existing type of the scan definition is left unchanged.
A hashtable of properties which define the scan. The required/valid keys depend on the value of -type.
If not specified, the existing properties of the scan definition are left unchanged. If specified, replaces the existing properties entirely, rather than merging into them.
The location of the scan targets.
This value cannot actually be changed once a scan definition is created; if not specified, the existing locationType of the scan definition is left unchanged.
The credentials used to run the scan and access the targets, when scanning a database or from a list of targets, as an array of hashtables.
Each hashtable defines name, type (ACCOUNT or UNMANAGED_ACCOUNT), properties (a hashtable containing account_id), and optionally defaultAccount.
If not specified, the existing credentials of the scan definition are left unchanged. If specified, replaces the existing credentials entirely.

maml:description.maml:para: Check discovered account existence
Check discovered account existence

-type and -subtype both provide tab-completion (sourced from Get-DMDiscoveredAccountTypeMap), with -subtype's completions narrowing to those valid for whichever -type has already been typed. A warning is emitted (for both the single and multiple parameter sets) if the supplied identifiers do not look like a match for the given Type/SubType, per Get-DMDiscoveredAccountTypeMap - any keys you provide are always included as-is; nothing is stripped or rejected.
The account type
The account subtype
List of properties that define the uniqueness of the account, as a hashtable.
The required/valid keys depend on the value provided for -type/-subtype - see Get-DMDiscoveredAccountTypeMap for reference.
The external id of the account
a collection of accounts to query.
each account must be a hashtable containing type, subType, identifiers & externalId keys, in the format expected by the API.
New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject can be used to create correctly structured account objects to pass as this parameter's value.

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- Example 1 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> Test-DMDiscoveredLocalAccount -type Windows -subtype Domain -identifiers @{address='win-computer.cyber-ark.com'; username='admin'} -externalId "user_account_5924"

dev:remarks.maml:para: Checks for the existence of the specified account

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- Example 2 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> $accounts = @( New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject -type windows -subType loosely -identifiers @{address='win-computer.cyber-ark.com'; username='admin'} -externalId user_account_5924 New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject -type mac -subType loosely -identifiers @{address='mac-computer.cyber-ark.com'; username='root'} -externalId user_account_1132 ) PS C:\> Test-DMDiscoveredLocalAccount -accounts $accounts

dev:remarks.maml:para: Uses New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject to build an array of correctly structured account objects, and checks for the existence of all of them in a single request.

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- Example 3 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: PS C:\> $accounts = @( New-DMDiscoveredAccountObject -type AWS -subType Password -identifiers @{username='someuser'} -externalId aws_account_1 ) PS C:\> Test-DMDiscoveredLocalAccount -accounts $accounts

dev:remarks.maml:para: Builds & checks the existence of a discovered AWS account - a Type/SubType whose identifiers are not the common address/username shape.
